statement: For C82's actual null lifted triangulation, restriction of the original relative centralizer to the compact full skeleton plus original circle has an explicitly characterized embedding image and a global continuous section. Three labelled boundary vertices normalize each representative Jordan-domain Riemann map; radial correction matches the full boundary parameter, and conjugation by every original deck operator extends to all triangles, including orientation-reversing labels. The section fixes the identity. It gives the displayed topological product with C82's contractible pointwise skeleton stabilizer and an actual strong deformation retraction onto the section image.
depends_on: C81 exact original group and covering hypotheses; C82 null lifted triangulation and whole stabilizer contraction; verified Rado1923Variable closed-Jordan-domain parameter theorem; explicit labelled face extensions, exact intrinsic image conditions, original-circle pasting, full inverse topology, product maps and deformation proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), global section and compact-skeleton image topology for the remaining discrete-operator family deformation.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The conformal coordinate is fixed with its exact transport maps and metric comparison. Riemann maps are normalized at all three specified boundary vertices; the Radial correction supplies the complete boundary restriction. Deck operators are used only in actual conjugation formulas, with trivial triangle stabilizers proved from the covering. Nullity controls all infinitely many original image faces, and compact-disk inverse convergence is proved explicitly.
computational_checks: This is a topological construction with no new numerical or finite counterexample. Structural checks validate metadata, unique equation labels and literal TeX control sequences. The exact extension, inverse, operator and homotopy formulas are proved in the text.

General C12 remains open at the controlled deformation of that image, or the C88 cutoff to compact quotient support. Accepted C81-C88 and shared assembly files remain unchanged.
